blocks.text: Open Displays & Layout in Computer Management or Display in desktop settings. The wdisplays interface controls arrangement, scale, rotation and modes advertised by the compositor. Keep a known working display enabled while making changes.

The session output watcher reconciles host display policy and hotplug state. Refresh Outputs requests its existing refresh route. GTK4 scales with the Wayland output; use Help's text-size controls for reading size rather than overriding global GTK scale variables.

If a mode produces a black screen, use another working display or sign out normally where possible. Record connector and mode details before changing policy. A DRM 'Device or resource busy' message alone does not identify the cause; do not apply global graphics workarounds without target evidence.
Make one display change at a time

Record the current connector, resolution, refresh rate and scale before changing them. Choose only modes advertised for that output; inspect the full width × height and refresh rate instead of assuming two similarly named modes are identical. Keep a working keyboard and display available.

A manual display adjustment and the managed output policy are separate. If an arrangement changes after reconnecting a monitor or signing in, record when it changes and inspect the selected host policy. Do not disable the output watcher or add global graphics flags before identifying the owning setting.
